invariants: Preserve both live quest ids, all objective ids, objective tasks, graph edges, battle opponents, scaling, coordinates, profession-specific reward chests, AI stats, jutsu mechanics, and AI profile rule logic unless explicitly changed below.
Drowned Fleet is out of scope.
Player-facing prose must contain no em dash or en dash.
Top-level quest sceneBackground must be set deliberately during implementation rather than preserving the current empty string.
Ghost Ship combatants migrate to the shared AI pool according to state/ghost_ship_shared_pool_migration.json; the previous 29-jutsu rename plan is superseded.
Legacy-only Ghost Ship jutsu are unequipped but not deleted in this pass. Deletion requires a later dependency audit.
The Skyglass Crown and Fragment of the Skyglass Crown keep their current live item ids and mechanics; this pass renames/rethemes those records rather than replacing them.

6Ri-W5TtUrEMWpyYlnf_F.name: Ghost Ship (Gather)
6Ri-W5TtUrEMWpyYlnf_F.description: The legendary Ghost Ship has returned, a warship thought destroyed decades ago now hanging over the coast on a lattice of impossible seals. Board it before it vanishes, learn what the Skyglass Core preserved, and escape with whatever the lost project still guards.
6Ri-W5TtUrEMWpyYlnf_F.successDescription: The Ghost Ship fades from the sky as suddenly as it came. What you recovered is real. So are the signs that something aboard still remembers the old mission.

HckXVOf-qk6ESU9t5rxLh.description: The legendary Ghost Ship has returned, a warship thought destroyed decades ago now hanging over the coast on a lattice of impossible seals. Board it before it vanishes, learn what the Skyglass Core preserved, and escape with whatever the lost project still guards.

d_intro.description: The Ghost Ship appears without approach. One moment the moon is clear; the next, a black hull hangs beneath it, seal-light burning through the keel where the sea should be. Every record says the vessel was destroyed decades ago. Tonight it lowers a gangplank.

d_gang.description: At the top of the gangplank, the Deck Warden takes shape from pale script and old armor. Behind him, two seal charges hum beside the rail. His face is young. The uniform is generations out of date.

b_gang.description: Break the Deck Warden and the unstable charges guarding the entry.

r_gang.description: The Deck Warden drives you back over the rail. The ship does not pursue. Board again.

c_climb.description: Climb the anchor chain beneath the hull. The metal is warm with chakra, and every few breaths the ship seems to lose weight beneath your hands.

d_bilgein.description: Inside the lower hull, cracked seal-lines leak pale chakra into soaked timber and cable. The wreckage gathers itself around a half-formed human outline, as if the ship remembers a crew member badly. The Core Horror turns toward you.

b_bilge.description: The Core Horror tears itself free of the lower hull.

r_bilge.description: The Horror collapses over you in timber, cable, and cold chakra. When the ship rebuilds the breach, you are back outside it. Climb again.

d_parley.description: The Oathkeeper appears at the rail in an officer's coat faded by no weather. Pale seal-script passes through his hands. 'Answer true and walk aboard oathbound. Answer false and prove yourself by force. What does every traveler keep while every journey spends it?'

d_oathpass.description: 'Time.' For the first time, the Oathkeeper smiles. 'We had plenty of that.' He steps aside as seal-lines brighten beneath your feet. 'Oath accepted. The Captain will know.'

d_duel.description: 'Wrong.' The Oathkeeper draws a narrow blade and salutes. 'Then show me what the living learned while we were gone.'

b_herald.description: The Oathkeeper lowers his blade and begins the test.

r_parley.description: The Oathkeeper's blade finds you three times. He lowers it, unimpressed, and the ship's seals cast you back outside. Call again.

d_deck.description: The deck is too wide for the hull beneath it. Empty mess tables are laid for a meal no one has touched, while crew afterimages repeat their stations between pulses of seal-light. Three routes open ahead: the chart room, the sealed hold, or the long walk to the helm.

d_quarters.description: The Wayfinder looks up from charts layered with decades of corrections. Some mark villages that did not exist when his uniform was new. Others show mountains from angles no ground navigator could have drawn. 'Still no home port,' he says.

b_nav.description: The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.

r_quarters.description: Ink, seal-light, and false horizons swallow the room. When your sight returns, you are back on the deck. The chart room waits.

d_map.description: Among the impossible routes is an old field cache, marked before the ship vanished. The ink is decades old. The Wayfinder's newest corrections are not.

d_hold.description: Rows of sealed crates fill the hold. Inventory slates show the same quantities checked again and again across decades. The Arsenal Keeper stands among untouched rations and medicine. 'Nothing leaves unaccounted.'

b_qm.description: The Arsenal Keeper raises the counterweight maul.

r_hold.description: The maul ends the argument. The ship's seals cast you back to the deck while the hold closes behind him. Descend again.

d_helm.description: Two Deck Wardens hold the approach to the helm. Beyond them, the command dais glows around a fractured ring of white crystal.

b_helm.description: The Wardens bar the last steps to the helm.

r_helm.description: The Wardens hold the passage and the command dais remains beyond them. Try again.

d_helm_oath.description: Even the oathbound are tested before the helm. Two Deck Wardens step into the passage as the seal-lines beneath them flare white.

b_helm_oath.description: The Wardens bar the way, oath or no oath.

r_helm_oath.description: The Wardens hold. The oath remains recorded. Try the passage again.

d_riddle.description: A notation along the route sheet reads: 'Where the cliff drinks and the stone keeps watch, the cache sleeps beneath the watcher's shadow.' Three coves match part of the description.
choices: The cove beneath the stone shrine
The cove with the split cliff
The open beach past the reef

d_wrong1.description: You dig until the tide reaches your knees. Broken seal plates and driftwood, nothing more. The watcher's shadow falls elsewhere.

d_wrong2.description: Only reef stone and an old anchor frame lie beneath the sand. Re-read the route sheet.

c_dig.description: Dig beneath the stone watcher's shadow before the tide shifts.

d_guardian.description: Your shovel strikes metal. Sand bursts outward as the Sentinel unfolds from a buried seal frame, armor plated with shell and stone around the cache.

b_guardian.description: The Sentinel rises between you and the cache.

r_dig.description: The Sentinel drives you into the sand and settles back over the buried seal frame. The cache remains.

d_claim_A.description: The Sentinel breaks apart into sand and fading script. Beneath it sits a sealed field cache stamped with the same Skyglass project mark etched into the ship's keel.

w_A.description: You recover a field cache left before the Ghost Ship vanished. Its supplies are old. The seal keeping them preserved is still active.

d_crates.description: Unsealed supplies can be carried out now. Behind them, a black reinforcement door bears the Captain's personal seal. Nothing in the hold looks used, only counted.

d_escape.description: You shoulder a supply crate and head for the rail. The Deck Warden reforms in the exit path, chakra hook already in hand.

b_escape.description: The Deck Warden bars the exit one last time.

r_escape.description: The Warden catches you before the rail and drags the crate back into the hold. The exit remains.

d_claim_B1.description: You reach the shore with the crate as the Ghost Ship begins to lift away. The haul is modest, but real.

w_B1.description: You chose the sure supplies and escaped before the ship vanished again.

d_vault.description: The Captain's seal breaks. Cold wind spills from a room without windows. The First Blade steps out in the uniform of a dead era, twin cleavers forming from the gale. 'Finally,' he says. 'Something new.'

b_fm.description: The First Blade steps through the broken seal.

r_vault.description: The gale folds the room around you. When the ship releases you, the Captain's seal is whole again. Break it once more.

d_claim_B2.description: The wind dies with the First Blade. The restricted vault stands open, revealing equipment the crew itself was never meant to touch.

w_B2.description: You broke the Captain's private seal and claimed what the ship had guarded from its own crew.

d_king.description: At the command dais stands the Captain, almost solid beneath the core-link seals. An empty ring of white crystal hangs above him. 'They built this ship to cross any wall and outlast any siege,' he says. 'No one asked what outlasting everything would cost.'

b_king.description: The Captain steps down from the command dais.

r_king.description: The Captain ends the duel and the helm flashes white. A moment later you are back at the approach, the challenge still waiting.

d_claim_C.description: The Captain lowers his weapon. 'The ship died once. Skyglass disagreed.' Behind him, the command stores unlock.

w_C.description: You cross the Ghost Ship from rail to helm and defeat the Captain it remembers. The command stores open, but the ship itself shows no sign of ending.

d_kingoath.description: The Captain turns before you reach the dais. The Oathkeeper's mark burns across the floor. White crystal rises from the control ring and closes around his brow. 'The order was preserve command, preserve crew, keep the vessel airborne until the mission ended. The mission never ended.'

b_kingE.description: The Skyglass Crown completes itself. Every seal on the Ghost Ship answers at once as the Crowned Captain steps down.

r_king_oath.description: The Crowned Captain breaks your guard and the helm flashes white. The oath remains recorded. When you return to the dais, he is waiting at full synchronization.

d_claim_Co.description: White crystal fractures from his brow and hangs in the air as fading shards. The Captain drops to one knee. 'Now you understand why they feared us.' The command stores open behind him as the ship begins to fade.

w_Co.description: You defeat the Ghost Ship's most complete memory of its Captain. The vessel slips out of the world again, still following a mission no living shinobi remembers.

XhilCv1Hq4eNt-Wddok-m.description: A concentrated restorative sealed for long-duration chakra operations aboard the Ghost Ship. One dose restores the body as quickly as it drains the bottle.

storyCanon.publicLegend: The Ghost Ship is called a ghost because it should not exist. Official records say the experimental warship was destroyed decades ago, yet it periodically materializes in the sky with no visible approach and vanishes again just as suddenly.
storyCanon.project: The vessel was a forbidden shinobi engineering project built around a chakra-reactive Skyglass Core. A hull-wide seal lattice let it ignore terrain, remain airborne and strike from directions conventional defenses could not cover.
storyCanon.crewFate: The Core was ordered to preserve command continuity and crew function through catastrophic damage. When the vessel was lost, the emergency lattice preserved chakra impressions instead of living bodies. The ship now reconstructs its crew as afterimages from stored patterns.
storyCanon.tragedy: The afterimages do not age because they are not biologically living. They can remember food, warmth, sleep, shore leave and ordinary life, but the ship continually rebuilds them for duty rather than letting them live those experiences. Some follow routine without understanding it; higher-fidelity impressions know exactly how much time has passed.
storyCanon.menace: The ship was feared because it could cross walls and mountains, appear above defended territory, and replace fallen crew from stored chakra patterns. Destroying a defender did not necessarily remove it from the next manifestation.
storyCanon.recurrence: Damage to the Skyglass emergency lattice leaves the vessel slipping in and out of stable space. It reappears along fragments of old routes when the Core accumulates enough chakra to reconstruct the ship and crew again.
storyCanon.captain: The Captain's normal reconstruction is highly stable but incomplete. The oathbound route causes the Core to rebuild the highest-fidelity command imprint through the Skyglass Crown, producing the Crowned Captain, who remembers the final project orders and understands what the crew became.
storyCanon.crown: The Skyglass Crown was the Captain's command interface with the Skyglass Core. Its fragments retain the crown's seal pattern, which is why five fragments can be restored into the complete item.

narrativeReveal.reveal: The ship materializes with no approach and is visibly held aloft by seal engineering.
The Deck Warden is physically young but wears a uniform generations out of date.
The Core can reconstruct bodies incorrectly, producing the Core Horror from hull material and a damaged crew pattern.
The Oathkeeper knows time has passed and distinguishes the living from the crew.
Charts contain decades of corrections, proving the ship has continued traveling after its supposed destruction.
Rations and medicine remain untouched while the Arsenal Keeper has counted them for decades.
The ship survived its destruction because Skyglass interpreted preservation orders literally.
The original mission never reached a termination state, so the Core continues rebuilding vessel, command and crew.
